parts.label: a
parts.technique: Calculate S_tt (sum of squares) for bivariate data
parts.reason: Computing S_tt is a summary-statistic sum-of-squares calculation analogous to S_xx in S2.3, and does not itself use the PMCC formula or regression line; it stands alone as a preliminary calculation, so it is not caught by the S2.2/S5.1 exclusions.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Calculate PMCC using the formula
parts.reason: S5.1 explicitly excludes calculation of correlation coefficients using the formula (calculator use only is allowed); this part requires substituting into the PMCC formula, so it is out.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Interpret correlation coefficient sign
parts.reason: This interpretation is based directly on the value of r found via the excluded formula method in (b); it depends on an out-of-spec part.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Find regression line equation
parts.reason: S2.2 explicitly excludes calculations involving regression lines.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Use regression line to estimate a value
parts.reason: Depends on the regression equation from (d), which is explicitly excluded by S2.2.

parts.label: f
parts.technique: Comment on validity of regression-based estimate
parts.reason: This relies on the out-of-spec regression estimate from (e); depends on an out-of-spec part.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Find median and quartiles from stem-and-leaf diagram
parts.reason: S2.3 covers measures of central tendency and variation including median and quartiles for grouped/ungrouped data.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Identify outliers using given rule
parts.reason: S2.4 explicitly covers recognising outliers using a rule specified in the question (e.g. Q1-1.5IQR).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Draw box and whisker plot with outliers
parts.reason: S2.1 covers box and whisker plots including outliers.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Compare distributions using measures of location/spread
parts.reason: S2.4 expects drawing simple inferences and interpretations from measures of central tendency and variation.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Histogram bar width/height from frequency density
parts.reason: S2.1 explicitly covers histograms and area representing frequency.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Linear interpolation for median from grouped data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly states linear interpolation to calculate percentiles from grouped data is expected.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Estimate mean and standard deviation from grouped frequency data
parts.reason: S2.3 covers calculation of standard deviation and mean from summary statistics/grouped data.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Describe skewness using mean/median comparison
parts.reason: S2.3/S2.4 cover interpretation of measures of central tendency and variation including skewness comparisons.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Estimate probability from grouped frequency table
parts.reason: S3.1 covers use of probability with discrete distributions; this is a straightforward relative-frequency probability calculation from grouped data.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Find probability from Venn diagram
parts.reason: S3.1/S3.2 cover use of Venn diagrams to calculate probabilities.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Use independence to find unknown probability then total probability
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly covers use of independent events formula P(A∩C)=P(A)P(C) and S3.2 covers Venn diagram probability calculations.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Conditional probability
parts.reason: S3.2 explicitly covers conditional probability formula P(A|B).

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Probability of independent repeated events
parts.reason: S3.1 covers independent events and multiplying probabilities for independent trials.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Find probability distribution from cumulative distribution function
parts.reason: S4.1 covers simple discrete probability distributions; deriving individual probabilities from a given cdf is within this scope and does not involve mean/variance calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Sum probabilities from a discrete distribution
parts.reason: Simple use of the probability distribution found in (a), within S4.1 scope.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Calculate Var(Y) where Y is a linear transformation of discrete random variable X
parts.reason: S4.1 explicitly excludes calculation of mean and variance of discrete random variables; this part requires E(X), E(X^2), Var(X) and Var(Y), squarely excluded.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Probability involving Y using values derived from Var(Y)/distribution of Y
parts.reason: This part uses the distribution of Y established via the excluded variance work in (c); depends on an out-of-spec part.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 explicitly covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Normal distribution probability calculation
parts.reason: S4.2 covers finding probabilities using the Normal distribution.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Apply Normal probabilities to a modelling/profit context
parts.reason: S4.2 covers using the Normal distribution as a model, and applying computed probabilities to a real-world costing scenario is a straightforward application, not requiring any excluded concept.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Find mean and standard deviation of Normal distribution from two probability statements
parts.reason: S4.2 guidance explicitly states questions may involve the solution of simultaneous equations to find Normal distribution parameters.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Reasoning about change in profit based on Normal distribution parameters
parts.reason: This is an interpretive comment building on the in-spec Normal distribution parameter-finding in (d), consistent with S4.2/S4.3 model interpretation.
